title: Mitigate cascade re-routing caused by stale policy shards and variant mapping drift
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity squeeze in us-east-1 on 2026-03-04 we observed cascading cross-region re-routes that amplified load on standby regions. Root cause was a combination of stale policy shards in the policy mesh and drift in model-variant mapping state between the central policy service and edge routers. The stale shard TTL inversion (policy shard TTL was longer than the variant mapping cache TTL) allowed routers to make decisions with old precedence information which caused repeated reroutes and variant mismatches. Impact: multiple large customers saw elevated latencies and a temporary increase in model-variant mismatch errors leading to degraded output quality and cost amplification from cross-region traffic.
timeline_comments: 2026-03-04 03:12 UTC - PagerDuty PD-2319 triggered: elevated 5xx and latency across us-east-1. Oncall (Diego Morales) started triage.

2026-03-04 03:27 UTC - Initial mitigation: reduce policy propagation frequency and pin policy mesh to last-known-good version (deploy rollback). Observed immediate reduction in reroute count but latency remained high.
2026-03-04 04:05 UTC - Discovered variant mapping drift between central policy service v2 and legacy edge agent. Edge agents still used older mapping with different fallback weights.
2026-03-04 05:10 UTC - Temporary protective rule: force local-variant affinity for in-flight sessions in affected POPs, preventing re-entrant reroutes.
2026-03-04 10:45 UTC - Full stabilization: coordinated cache flush and synchronous policy shard refresh across regions. Incident declared mitigated at 10:47 UTC.
2026-03-05 09:15 UTC - Post-incident sync with PM/Design/Support to collect customer reports and correlate with billing spikes. Action items captured and triage assigned.
root_cause: Two independent but compounding bugs: 1) policy mesh propagation produced shards with TTL semantics that allowed out-of-order precedence to persist on routers longer than variant cache lifetimes; 2) a recent change to variant-mapping serialization (PR #4217) introduced a subtle ordering change that caused some edge agents to interpret fallback weights incorrectly under TTL expiry, resulting in wrong-variant selection when a policy refresh arrived mid-request.
steps_taken: Rollback policy-propagation change to last-known-good commit (repo: infra/policy-mesh, PR reverted: #4302)
Force synchronous refresh: orchestrated cache flush across edge agents and central policy service using runbook run 2026-03-04-REFRESH-1
Applied short-term protective rule to pin affinity for active sessions for 10m windows in affected POPs
Added telemetry counters for shard TTL vs variant cache age to detect future inversion events
action_items: ENG-113211: Implement TTL contract enforcement in policy mesh so that shard TTL >= variant-cache TTL is detected and blocked (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-19)
ENG-113212: Add pre-deploy validation test to serialization change pipeline to verify stable fallback weight ordering across agent versions (owner: Malik Johnson, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-16)

ENG-113213: Roll out edge-agent upgrade with explicit mapping version tags and compatibility check; fail fast if central policy version is incompatible (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-02)
ENG-113214: Create automated end-to-end chaos test that simulates partial policy propagation and ensures no reentrant re-routing loops (owner: Sienna Park, estimate: 8, due: 2026-04-09)
ENG-113215: Dashboarding: add Grafana alert for shard/variant-age divergence and cross-region reroute spike (owner: Observability team, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-113216: Update runbook with explicit 'immediate protective rules' steps and post-incident checklist (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-14)
ENG-113217: Customer follow-up: CS to run impact reports for affected customers and provide remediation summary + credit where necessary (owner: Maria Gomez, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-113218: Architecture review to standardize TTL semantics across policy, routing, and variant stores (owner: Platform Architecture, due: 2026-04-16)
ENG-113219: Release note and communication: prepare postmortem summary for status.redwood.ai and mailing list (owner: Kate Lin, due: 2026-03-13)
review_notes: PM Review (Zoe Martinez): Confirmed customer-impact matrix and communication plan. Recommended prioritizing TTL enforcement and the runbook update.
Design Review (Alex Rivers): Suggested adding a small visual indicator in Console of 'policy freshness' per model route to help triage.
Security Review: Not required for code changes, but variant mapping serialization PR should be included in security scan pipeline.
notes_for_oncall: If similar alarm triggers, immediately set policy-propagation to read-only and run a synchronous policy shard refresh. If reroute spikes continue, enable protective local-variant affinity and escalate to Platform Architecture. Do not roll forward policy serialization changes without pre-deploy serialization compatibility checks.
